evidence: Ov. Pont. 1.3.36: immemorēs nōn sinit esse suī
Cic. Cat. 1.10: nōn feram, nōn patiar, nōn sinam (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: With an accusative and infinitive, or the subjunctive: sine sciam, let me know (Liv. 2.40.5, Lewis & Short).

terms.grammar: verb, impersonal, with the dative and an infinitive
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.103: lūdō autem et jocō ūtī illō quidem licet
terms.comment: “Am I allowed to?” is licetne?, and the answer licet, “yes, you may; all right”.

terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, with the dative
evidence: Cic. Fam. 13.71.1: nisi ego eī permīsissem
Gell. 5.2.3: haud umquam īnscendī sēsē ab aliō nisi ab rēge passus sit
terms.comment: Often with a negative: nōn patiar, I won’t have it.

phrases.latin: lūdō autem et jocō ūtī illō quidem licet, sed sīcut somnō et quiētibus cēterīs tum, cum gravibus sēriīsque rēbus satis fēcerimus
phrases.english: we may enjoy play and jokes, but as we enjoy sleep and other rest: when we have done enough serious and weighty work

phrases.latin: Concēde hūc ā foribus. — Fīat. — Etiam concēde hūc. — Licet.
phrases.english: Come away from the door. — All right. — Further this way. — OK.

phrases.latin: nesciō quā nātāle solum dulcēdine cūnctōs dūcit et immemorēs nōn sinit esse suī
phrases.english: by some sweetness or other our native soil draws us all and does not let us forget it
